heroDesc: Turn a file, folder, or stream into a link. Send it to a person with a browser, or an agent with a job to finish. No cloud-storage upload required.
heroNote: Free direct sharing · No account required · Apache-2.0 core
diagramFoot: Direct when possible. Relay when needed.
fact1: No cloud staging for direct transfers
workflowDesc: A photo album. A build artifact. A model checkpoint. The next step starts with the same command.
watchDesc: Publish new, settled child folders with --watch. A receiver uses --follow to pick up each delivery from one collection link. Ideal for build batches and generated artifacts.
watchNote: New folders only. Append-only delivery, not folder mirroring.
networkDesc: Cloud storage shouldn’t be a prerequisite for handing off a file. ffl connects the sender to the receiver, with a route that fits your network.
routeInternetNote: Direct TCP/QUIC between ffl clients; WebRTC for browsers. Public signaling and relay services may be used. HTTPS relay fallback helps when direct connections fail.
privacyTitle: Privacy is a choice you can see.
privacyInternet: Add --e2ee to encrypt file contents across relay fallback. Connection metadata remains visible. Direct sharing needs both ends online; cloud upload is a separate, optional feature.
agentsTitle:
Your agents make things.
Give them a way to deliver.
agentsDesc: Move a local model, a dataset, or a generated report between machines without a cloud bucket or a shared filesystem. Pass a link through your orchestrator; ffl carries the artifact.
cliDesc: Share files or stdin. Read the link from --json, track progress with --hook, and stream downloads to --stdout. Native TCP/QUIC helps ffl clients move large payloads directly.
mcpTitle: A transfer tool for your agent.
mcpDesc: Connect the companion ffl-mcp server to an MCP-capable host. Let agents share outputs and download inputs through tools, then hand the same link to a human.
embedDesc: Use structured events and host-provided file sources to integrate transfers into your own application. Your app owns the interface and lifecycle; ffl handles delivery.
installDesc: Install the CLI on the sender. Your recipient can just open the link.
installUnixNote: Native builds: Linux x86_64; macOS Intel and Apple Silicon. For Linux ARM64, use APE.
faq1Q: Is there a file-size limit or a cloud quota?
faq1A: Direct sharing has no cloud-storage quota and requires no account. Real limits are your network, filesystem, receiver, and sender availability. Relay providers may impose their own limits. Optional server upload has separate account and plan limits.
faq2Q: Does the sender need to stay online?
faq2A: Yes, for direct and live relayed sharing. Keep ffl and the source files available until the receiver finishes. If both sides cannot be online together, optional --upload stores the file temporarily on a server and requires an account and the Upload addon.
faq3A: E2EE is opt-in: add --e2ee for file-content encryption across direct and relay paths, and receive with ffl or its browser page. Metadata remains visible, and E2EE alone is not a guarantee against active man-in-the-middle attacks. LAN links use HTTP; use them on trusted networks. See the README for authentication and the security model.
faq4Q: Is ffl an agent framework or a sync drive?
faq4A: ffl is the transfer layer. Your agent host or orchestrator decides what to send, exchanges the link, and manages the process. --watch publishes new direct child folders after they settle; existing folders and later edits are not mirrored. --follow receives each new delivery.

agentComment: # Worker A publishes its output and structured events.

agentNote: The next worker downloads the artifact and continues its task. Keep the sender process alive until delivery completes.

lanNote: No public tunnel. LAN links use HTTP: use a trusted network and --e2ee for file contents. Tunnel preferences persist; restore internet sharing with --preferred-tunnel default.
routeLocalNote: Explicit LAN mode binds to a local IP and bypasses public tunnel routing. Both devices must be able to reach that address. Allow the listening port through the firewall.
routeLocalFallback: ↳ Direct LAN route · no public tunnel
privacyLocal: LAN links use HTTP. Add --e2ee for file-content encryption; the page and metadata remain unencrypted. Use a trusted network. The tunnel choice is remembered for future runs.
